title: Election Results Atlas
text: The atlas compares election results at the geographic level available for each state. It starts with North Carolina, where the State Board of Elections publishes precinct-level November results.

title: Election Results Atlas
text:
Available states

North Carolina: November 2026 county and precinct results

The North Carolina page begins with a county map and includes the same precinct-level source data used by the statewide analysis.

title: North Carolina
text:
The map shows the Democratic margin in percentage points by county: D+ means Roy Cooper led Michael Whatley in that county.

pal <- colorBin(
  palette = c("#b2182b", "#ef8a62", "#f7f7f7", "#67a9cf", "#2166ac"),
  bins = c(-100, -20, -5, 5, 20, 100),
  domain = county_map$margin_2026,
  na.color = "#bdbdbd"
)

leaflet(county_map, options = leafletOptions(zoomSnap = 0.25)) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(margin_2026),
    fillOpacity = 0.82,
    color = "white",
    weight = 0.7,
    label = ~paste0(
      county_name, ": ",
      if_else(margin_2026 > 0, "D+", "R+"),
      abs(round(margin_2026, 1))
    ),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#333333",
      fillOpacity = 0.95,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal,
    values = ~margin_2026,
    title = "Democratic margin",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "%")
  )

title: North Carolina
text:
County shift from 2024
The chart compares each county’s 2026 Senate margin with its 2024 presidential margin. Positive values mean a more Democratic result in 2026 relative to 2024.

plot <- ggplot(county_comparison,
               aes(x = margin_2024, y = margin_2026,
                   text = county_name,
                   color = swing)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed",
              color = "gray50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray70") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#b2182b", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#2166ac",
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Senate margin vs. 2024 presidential margin",
    x = "2024 Harris margin (percentage points)",
    y = "2026 Cooper margin (percentage points)",
    color = "Swing toward Democrats"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(plot, tooltip = "text")

title: North Carolina
text:
Data coverage

2026 source: NCSBE precinct results, November 3, 2026
2024 source: NCSBE precinct results, November 5, 2024
2026 geographic scale: precinct results aggregated to counties
Future geographic scale: Census or NCSBE precinct boundaries
Candidates shown: Roy Cooper vs. Michael Whatley, and Kamala Harris vs. Donald Trump

The underlying 2026 and 2024 files are stored in data/north-carolina/2026-11-03/ and data/north-carolina/2024-11-05/.

title: Who Moved to Sarasota County?
text:
These estimates describe people who lived outside Sarasota County one year ago and reported Sarasota County as their current residence.

ggplot(movers_by_origin, aes(x = fct_reorder(movement, people), y = people)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(people)), hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "People moving to Sarasota County, 2024",
    subtitle = "Residence one year ago, ACS 1-year estimates",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated number of people"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

title: Who Moved to Sarasota County?
text:
Age of people moving

ggplot(age_data, aes(x = factor(age, levels = age_groups),
                     y = people,
                     fill = movement)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Age groups of people who moved to Sarasota County",
    subtitle = "2024 ACS 1-year estimates",
    x = "Age",
    y = "Estimated number of people",
    fill = "Where they moved from"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")

title: Who Moved to Sarasota County?
text:
Sex of people moving

ggplot(sex_data, aes(x = movement, y = people, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Sex of people moving to Sarasota County",
    subtitle = "2024 ACS 1-year estimates",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated number of people",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")








Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 ACS 1-year estimates, accessed through Census Reporter. Estimates have margins of error and should not be interpreted as exact counts.
